observation_text: Child was asked to help clean up toys after playtime.
behavior: Child picked up one toy and then sat down.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make cleanup more fun for them?
general_support_idea: Incorporate songs or games during cleanup time.

observation_text: Child was asked to put their shoes away before snack time.
behavior: Child put one shoe away but left the other on the floor.
caregiver_response: Caregiver reminded to finish the task.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can help encourage completing tasks?

observation_text: Child was asked to help set the table for lunch.
behavior: Child set one plate and then got distracted by a toy.
caregiver_response: Caregiver redirected attention to the table.
suggested_followup_question: How can I keep them focused on tasks?
general_support_idea: Use timers to add a fun element to tasks.

observation_text: Child was asked to clean up their art supplies after finishing a project.
behavior: Child started cleaning but then decided to draw instead.
suggested_followup_question: What can motivate them to finish cleaning up?
general_support_idea: Make cleanup part of the art process.

observation_text: Child was asked to put their books back on the shelf after reading.
antecedent: Child had just finished reading a book.
behavior: Child placed a few books on the shelf but left some on the floor.
caregiver_response: Caregiver prompted to finish the job.
suggested_followup_question: What methods can help them remember to organize?
general_support_idea: Create a routine for tidying up after activities.

observation_text: Child was asked to help clean up after snack time. They pushed the chair instead of picking up the crumbs.
behavior: Child pushed the chair across the floor.
consequence: Child noticed they could reach the toy on the shelf by standing on the chair.
possible_trigger: Desire to play with the toy instead of cleaning.
caregiver_response: Encouraged them to come down safely.
suggested_followup_question: What do you think would help make cleanup easier next time?
general_support_idea: Offering fun cleanup songs or games could help make it enjoyable.

observation_text: Child was playing outside and was asked to come inside. They kept running around the yard.
antecedent: Transitioning from outdoor play to indoor activities.
behavior: Child ignored the request and continued playing.
consequence: Child stopped running when a friend called them to join a game.
possible_trigger: Desire to continue playing with friends.
caregiver_response: Joined in the game but eventually came inside when everyone did.
suggested_followup_question: How can I help them transition from outdoor to indoor play more smoothly?
general_support_idea: Creating a routine for transitions can help children understand what's expected.

observation_text: Child was asked to help pick up toys in the living room. They picked up a few toys but started playing with them instead.
antecedent: Toys were scattered around the living room after playtime.
behavior: Child started playing with the toys instead of putting them away.
consequence: Child ended up reading a book on the floor instead of helping.
caregiver_response: Suggested they pick up one toy before they could play with it.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can I use to keep them focused on the cleanup task?
general_support_idea: Setting a timer for cleanup can create a sense of urgency.

observation_text: Child was in a crowded store and refused to hold the caregiver's hand while walking through the aisles.
antecedent: Busy environment with many people around.
behavior: Child suddenly let go of the caregiver's hand and ran ahead.
consequence: Child bumped into a display and startled, then returned to the caregiver.
emotion_context: Feeling overwhelmed in a crowded space.
caregiver_response: Reassured them and held their hand tighter until they felt secure.
suggested_followup_question: What can I do to help them feel safe in busy places?
general_support_idea: Practicing holding hands in quieter settings can build comfort.

observation_text: Child was asked to help clean up after arts and crafts. They locked themselves in the bathroom instead.
behavior: Child locked the door and refused to come out when asked.
consequence: Child eventually came out after a few minutes and apologized.
possible_trigger: Desire for quiet time or to avoid cleanup.
caregiver_response: Checked the door and talked calmly about the cleanup.
suggested_followup_question: How can I encourage them to participate in cleanup without feeling overwhelmed?
general_support_idea: Offering choices in cleanup tasks may help them feel more in control.
